text: Director, Moulton Niguel Water District
Water is life. Water is my life.

My focus:
Infrastructure. Interagency relationships. Reliability. Water quality. Fire protection. Low monthly bills.
My qualifications:
Proven leadership with 50 years’ experience—8 years as your MNWD Director. Recognized technical expertise as Principal Water Engineer (City of Anaheim, retired) and Registered Civil Engineer. Advanced training with BA Biology, MS Civil/Environmental Engineering, highest level in water/wastewater operation certifications.
Deep experience with 50 years’ mastering engineering, water quality, public policy. 36 years as an MNWD customer. Record of accomplishments as your Director:
Safety and reliability through fast-tracked emergency leak response, expanded valve maintenance program, secured fire hydrant upkeep. Fiscal responsibility proven by voting against Director pay increases, declined one for self, approved smart budgets for infrastructure upgrades. Community involvement and innovation by establishing vital fire-protection helipad and next-generation water reuse projects. Advocacy through approved rate structure securing long-term water quality and reliability. Participated in Naturescape Conservation Program at own expense.
My community commitment:
Local leadership with OC Infrastructure Report, past President of OC Water Association, board member Lake Mission Viejo Association. Personal civic support proudly funding Moulton Museum, Niguel Botanical Preserve, OC Coastkeeper’s, Mission Viejo HS, Model UN 4-year board member.

text: Appointed Moulton Niguel Water District Director
As your Director on the Moulton Niguel Water District Board, I am committed to:
Safeguarding our vital water resources
Maintaining the lowest rates possible
Ensuring financial accountability

Throughout my service on the Board, I have applied my 30+ years of business experience to champion operational efficiency and fiscal responsibility. A longtime Laguna Niguel resident, I intimately understand the importance of delivering safe, high-quality, and reliable drinking water and wastewater services to our community.

My leadership on the District Board builds on a deep foundation of public service, including my time serving on the 2023-24 Orange County Grand Jury, where I co-authored a landmark report on optimizing South County water and wastewater systems. That critical work laid the groundwork for regional realignments that save taxpayers money and improve local infrastructure stewardship.
I respectfully ask for your vote to continue serving as your Moulton Niguel Water District Director.

text: Family Caregiver

For more than 22 years, I have proudly called Aliso Viejo home. As a longtime resident, parent, ratepayer, and business professional, I have a personal investment in our community and the essential services we rely on every day.
Water is more than a utility; it is essential to our families, our health, and our future. Residents deserve clear information, timely communication, responsible stewardship, and accountability.

I bring more than 20 years of experience in corporate marketing, digital strategy, project management, and business consulting. My career has required me to analyze data, manage budgets, measure results, solve complex problems, and adapt thoughtfully to change.
Today, my greatest responsibility is serving as a full-time family caregiver, which has deepened my commitment to protecting the health and future of our community.

If elected, I will advocate for transparency, fiscal responsibility, and meaningful community engagement. I will ask thoughtful questions, evaluate the facts, and work to ensure residents understand water quality, infrastructure investments, and how ratepayer dollars are spent.
It would be an honor to earn your trust and serve the community my family and I have proudly called home for more than two decades.

text: Utility Project Manager

I hold a degree in Mechanical Engineering from the California Maritime Academy and have worked in construction management for more than a decade. Throughout my career, I have managed projects involving water, sewer, and gas infrastructure, wind turbines, houses, apartments, and coffee shops. These projects have taught me the importance of collaboration and bringing people with different priorities together to achieve a common goal. That means listening, solving problems, balancing competing interests, and building solutions that everyone can support.

I have broad experience scheduling budgeting, and coordinating complex projects, keeping them on time, and on budget. This means managing expectations, securing commitments, communicating openly and honestly, and providing realistic forecasts. I help teams make informed decisions and deliver results.
These are the skills I want to bring to our water board.

Above all, I believe trust is the foundation of effective leadership. I follow through on my commitments, speak up when something needs to be challenged, take responsibility when things don't go as planned and don't shy away from difficult decisions or tough conversations.
You can count on me to keep our water clean, safe, reliable and affordable, not just today, but for many years to come.

text: City Councilmember

I’ve lived in our community since 1977, when my husband, Jack, a United States Marine Corps pilot, was assigned to Marine Corps Air Station El Toro. We raised our three children here and have nine young grandchildren.

As a City Councilmember, I’ve delivered results:
Protected water quality by fighting water waste and urban runoff 90% of all City irrigation uses recycled water and drip irrigation Smart irrigation controllers ensure the City’s watering schedule adjusts based on weather conditions, reducing water waste Balanced budgets
Maintained strong reserves, AAA bond ratings
Reformed pension formulas, reduced unfunded liabilities Ended an unfair taxation program

I deeply believe in serving our community, having been the American Cancer Society’s Relay for Life Co-Chair, PTA President at 3 schools, a Saddleback College Foundation Governor, and volunteer at Compass Bible Church. I’d like to continue serving our community at the Moulton Niguel Water District.

If you elect me as your Moulton Niguel Water District Director, I’ll bring my results-oriented leadership to:
Protect our water supply
Maintain low water rates
Improve efficiency to keep costs down
Expand our local water storage
Enhance our critical water infrastructure
Pay down pension debt to protect retirees, employees, and ratepayers
I will always be accessible to you. Contact me at (949) 899-1886 or trishkelley1@gmail.com.
I would be honored to have your vote. trishkelley.com

text: Water Business Manager

As a water industry professional and long time Aliso Viejo resident and ratepayer, I am running for the Moulton Niguel Water District Board to help deliver reliable, high-quality water at the lowest practical cost.

I serve as Water Business Manager at Mesa Water District, focusing on accountability and efficiency for ratepayers. I oversee independent audits of finance, customer service, information technology, safety, and performance—helping keep the agency among Orange County’s most efficient.

I have previously served on MNWD’s Citizens Advisory Committee, as a Board Member for the Aliso Viejo Community Association and Aliso Viejo Little League, and was appointed Planning Commissioner for the City of Aliso Viejo. I currently serve as a volunteer umpire for Aliso Viejo Little League, supporting fairness and positive experiences for local youth.
Guided by the call to serve others, I will work to steward MNWD’s resources faithfully for every ratepayer.
If elected, I will prioritize:
Transparency, efficiency, and accountability
Water-supply reliability through a strong portfolio of supply options
Strong fiscal oversight to protect ratepayers and keep service affordable
I bring hands-on water industry experience, community involvement, and a commitment to serve you, the ratepayer. I respectfully ask for your vote.
